subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Should OpenClaw establish a native capability-scoped credential broker for agent-executed operations, and should that contract live in core or the plugin SDK?
rationale: Current main intentionally provides separate SecretRef, sentinel, redaction, generic exec-hook, and sandbox primitives but does not promise agent-inaccessible credentials; maintainers must select the authorization model, supported adapters, and permanent owner.

options.title: Core broker seam
options.body: Add a generic core security contract for named capabilities and approved adapters, while allowing plugins to supply credential providers.

options.title: Plugin SDK broker
options.body: Standardize plugin-owned credential resolution and operation authorization with core enforcing hook order and result redaction.

options.title: No native broker
options.body: Require separate-user, container, or external proxy isolation for strong guarantees and document current primitives as mitigations only.

recommendation.title: Core broker seam
recommendation.body: Add a generic core security contract for named capabilities and approved adapters, while allowing plugins to supply credential providers.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS and feature history place the secrets runtime and its security guarantees under this team.
